title: Shakshuka
subtitle: Eggs poached in spiced tomato and pepper sauce
excerpt: Eggs poached directly in a thick, vibrantly spiced sauce of tomatoes, peppers, cumin, and paprika. A dish of North African and Middle Eastern origin, eaten for breakfast or brunch, quick enough for a weeknight, and as satisfying as cooking gets.

recipe.sourceNotes: Shakshuka is eaten across North Africa and the Middle East, with the name derived from Arabic meaning mixture or all mixed up. Its most celebrated version is Tunisian, where it is considered a national dish, though Israeli versions (brought by Libyan and Tunisian Jewish immigrants in the mid-twentieth century) have made it internationally famous. The dish is built around a base tomato and pepper sauce deeply flavoured with cumin, paprika, and often harissa, into which eggs are cracked and left to poach with the lid on. The technique is simple; the quality depends on the sauce. The sauce should be thick, concentrated, and well seasoned before the eggs go in; a thin sauce will not support the eggs properly and they will sink and overcook.

content.text: Cook the sauce until it is thick and concentrated before adding the eggs; add a splash of water if it sticks. Make a well for each egg with a spoon before cracking it in. Fit the lid tightly and use a wide, flat-bottomed pan so the eggs are all exposed to the same temperature. Check at 5 minutes: the whites should be just set and the yolks still runny.

Heat the oil in a wide frying pan with a lid over medium heat. Cook the onion and peppers for 10 minutes until very soft. Add the garlic, cumin, paprika, and chilli flakes. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add the tinned tomatoes. Season with salt. Cook over medium heat, stirring occasionally, for 10 to 15 minutes until the sauce is thick and has reduced significantly.

Make 4 wells in the sauce with a large spoon. Crack an egg into each well. Cover tightly and cook over medium-low heat for 5 to 6 minutes until the whites are just set and the yolks remain runny. Scatter with fresh coriander and serve immediately from the pan with bread.
